edges.rationale: Direct rivals in frontier model training and enterprise API market. Anthropic was founded in 2021 by former OpenAI research leadership.
Frontier model competition (Claude vs Gemini family) across both API and consumer surfaces.
Frontier model competition (GPT vs Gemini) across API, consumer, and enterprise product lines.
Frontier model competition; xAI was founded by Musk after his OpenAI board departure and lawsuit against OpenAI.
Frontier model competition (Claude vs Grok).
Compete on frontier capability; philosophical opposition on release strategy (closed weights vs Meta's open-weight Llama family).
Frontier capability competition plus opposing release philosophies (Anthropic closed + safety-first vs Meta open-weight).
Frontier competition between Google's proprietary Gemini and Meta's open-weight Llama family.
Co-signers of the 2023 Statement on AI Risk (organized by CAIS, endorsed by FLI leadership). Aligned on framing existential risk as a policy priority.
Shared framing of alignment as a technical prerequisite to safe deployment. Overlapping researcher network and public statements.
FLI has repeatedly amplified MIRI positions in coalition letters and pause/moratorium advocacy.
Long-running digital-rights coalition partners; regularly co-sign amicus briefs and open letters on surveillance and platform regulation applied to AI.
Coalition partners on open-web and open-source AI advocacy; overlapping policy positions on transparency and interoperability.
Coalition partners on digital rights and open-source AI policy.
NIST AI Safety Institute and UK AISI announced a formal partnership on frontier model evaluation methods and shared testbeds (2024).
Peer academic AI research centers; jointly participate in national research funding calls and share safety-evaluation methodology.
National-security-focused policy think tanks with overlapping AI-safety research programs and mutual publication citations.
Anthropic is a founding member of Partnership on AI.
OpenAI is a founding member of Partnership on AI.
Google (DeepMind's parent) is a founding member of Partnership on AI.
Meta AI is a founding member of Partnership on AI.
Andreessen Horowitz participated in Anthropic's Series C funding round.
Andreessen Horowitz was among the lead investors in xAI's early funding rounds.
Y Combinator was OpenAI's early institutional backer; Sam Altman was YC president when OpenAI was founded (2015).
Future of Life Institute has provided grants to MIRI's technical alignment research program.
FLI has directed grants to Center for AI Safety's field-building and research programs.
Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy is the canonical corporate expression of 'race to build the safest AI' — capability-gated commitments as a competitive strategy.
Anthropic publicly supports capability-tiered regulation with obligations scaling to model power (RSP framework maps to this).
OpenAI's Superalignment / preparedness charter frames alignment as the central corporate technical priority.
DeepMind's alignment and safety papers position alignment as a core research pillar.
xAI released Grok model weights and repeatedly frames open-source release as competitive and epistemic virtue.
A16Z's 'Little Tech Agenda' explicitly champions open-source AI as pro-competition and pro-innovation.
Y Combinator's public policy stance favors open-source AI and startup access to frontier tools.
CAIS organized the 2023 Statement on AI Risk that framed extinction risk from AI as a global priority.
CAIS argues policymakers should act on AI risk under uncertainty rather than waiting for definitive proof of harm.
FLI's founding mission is preventing catastrophic and existential risks from advanced technology, with AI as central case.
FLI authored the 2023 'Pause Giant AI Experiments' open letter arguing for a moratorium.
MIRI's core research agenda is technical alignment — ensuring advanced AI reliably pursues intended goals.
MIRI has published extensively on recursive self-improvement as a mechanism for hard-takeoff scenarios.
EFF's AI work emphasizes transparency of training data and rights against opaque data collection.
AI Now Institute's core research program documents disparate AI impacts across demographic groups.
Access Now grounds its AI advocacy in an expansive rights-based definition of AI harm.
Mozilla champions open-source AI as continuous with its historical open-web mission.
NIST AI Risk Management Framework structures obligations by risk tier — the concrete US implementation of capability-graded governance.
The EU AI Act's risk-tier structure (prohibited / high / limited / minimal) is the flagship regulatory instantiation of capability-graded AI rules.
UK AISI's voluntary pre-deployment evaluation program is designed to make safety a competitive dimension for frontier labs.
OSTP coordinates the federal executive-branch AI governance agenda (Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights; EO 14110).
OECD AI Policy Observatory maintains the international framework and country-by-country AI policy comparison.
ISO/IEC JTC 1/SC 42 produces AI governance standards (ISO/IEC 42001 management system) organized by risk tier.
Stanford HAI's AI Index and policy briefs argue for evidence-based governance under uncertainty rather than waiting for proof of harm.
MIT CSAIL's research program centers scientific AI (AI for science, mathematical reasoning, materials discovery).
CSET's flagship research area is US-China AI competition and the strategic implications of the race.
RAND's AI research emphasizes societal resilience and defense adaptations to advanced AI.
Partnership on AI's mission is multi-stakeholder AI governance across industry, civil society, and academia.
Meta's Llama release strategy is the flagship corporate defense of open-weight frontier models.
Anthropic's public positions on frontier model release oppose open-sourcing weights of the most capable systems until safety cases are established.
xAI's public communications express skepticism of tiered-capability regulatory regimes as anticompetitive.
A16Z's Little Tech Agenda explicitly opposes tiered-capability rules that they argue would entrench incumbents.
Meta argues capability tiers as currently proposed would foreclose open-weight release paths for future frontier Llama models.
OpenAI publicly opposed the 2023 pause letter's moratorium framing, arguing continued deployment plus safety research is preferable.
Mozilla opposes opaque training-data provenance and campaigns for public data disclosure requirements.
EFF opposes granting legal personhood to AI systems as a governance mechanism, arguing it obscures human accountability.
Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy — capability-gated safety commitments framework.
OpenAI's Preparedness Framework — risk thresholds and mitigation obligations for frontier deployments.
Google DeepMind's Frontier Safety Framework — parallel to Anthropic's RSP and OpenAI's Preparedness Framework.
CAIS-organized 22-word Statement on AI Risk signed by AI researchers and public figures.
Future of Life Institute's Pause Giant AI Experiments open letter (March 2023).
NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 — the canonical US voluntary AI risk framework.
The EU AI Office is the enforcement body for the EU AI Act, which entered into force in 2024.
Blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights (October 2022), coordinating US federal AI-rights principles.
AI Now Institute's flagship annual report — recurring policy analysis of AI concentration and rights impacts.
CSET's US-China AI competition assessments are the reference documents for policymakers on the strategic race.
RAND report on securing frontier AI model weights against exfiltration by nation-state actors.
A16Z's Little Tech Agenda — the canonical pro-open-source, anti-tiered-regulation VC policy manifesto.
UK AI Safety Institute's frontier model evaluations report (post-Bletchley voluntary evaluation program).
OECD AI Principles — the foundational multilateral AI governance principles (adopted 2019, updated 2024).
Stanford HAI's AI Index — the reference dataset for AI progress and adoption metrics used by policy analysts.
PAI's Synthetic Media Framework — industry-civil-society compact on generative content provenance and disclosure.
